question: What claim about the range of languages is at stake in distinguishing heard and unheard forms of varied speech?
premises: Languages of varied form are present as a distinct class.
Some of those forms fall into the class of heard utterances.
Other forms fall into the class of unheard utterances.
inference: Varied languages include both heard and unheard forms.
uncertainties: The scope of 'languages' in this technical context is not fully determined.
plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms arise, both heard and unheard.
